ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all general partners, limited partners at or above the 10% internal monitoring threshold, and all UBOs against: UN Consolidated List; Global Affairs Canada sanctions under the Special Economic Measures Act and United Nations Act; OSFI financial sanctions lists; Interpol Red Notices; criminal records check for Customs AEO eligibility; FINTRAC suspicious transaction reporting obligations under section 7 of the PCMLTFA; domestic and foreign PEPs flagged for enhanced due diligence per FINTRAC Politically Exposed Persons Policy; ancillary reference to OFAC, UK ONSI, and HK lists for cross-border reputational risk. No statutory minimum capital is required for the LP.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Ontario Business Registry (ServiceOntario) operated by the Companies and Personal Property Security Branch (CPPSB), Ontario Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery; NUANS pre-clearance search report mandatory for Limited Partnership filings
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names may be registered in English, French, or bilingual form. The legal name must contain a mandatory element such as 'Limited Partnership', 'L.P.', 'société en commandite', or 's.e.c.'. Latin-script transliteration is required for names originating in non-Roman alphabets; UBO names must be romanized in a manner consistent with the passport and FINTRAC transcription standards. Names must be distinctive and not confusingly similar to existing Ontario or active federal names.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the CPPSB Director, the applicant may within 30 days submit a written request for reconsideration attaching the original NUANS report, a revised proposed name, and written submissions addressing the confusion grounds. If reconsideration is denied, the applicant may obtain judicial review before the Ontario Divisional Court under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, RSO 1990, c. J.1. Filing a new NUANS report restarts the 90-day validity window without court intervention.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally accepted as the registered office address for an Ontario limited partnership provided the address is a physical location in Ontario, service of process is accepted at that address, and the partnership's records are accessible there on demand; a post-office box alone is prohibited. However, for an AEO supply-chain audit consultancy, reliance on a virtual-only office substantially weakens Customs commercial-substance assessments under the CBSA Partners in Compliance framework, so a physical principal place of business in Ontario is recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 15% annual probability of an unannounced desk-level inspection of the registered office by Ontario authorities; approximately 8% probability of a CBSA site audit or pre-certification validation visit for an AEO-facing consultancy. The risk is higher than average because the business's core activity is Customs supply-chain security compliance.

incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; capital contributions are contractually agreed by partners. Escrow account requirements are not applicable to Ontario limited partnerships.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: WHEREAS the General Partner intends to form the Ontario Limited Partnership; NOW BE IT RESOLVED that (i) the draft limited partnership agreement is approved and the General Partner is authorized to execute and file the Application for Registration with ServiceOntario; (ii) the registered office at the principal address in Ontario is adopted; (iii) capital contributions in Schedule A are subscribed and funded according to the partnership agreement; (iv) [Name] is appointed initial agent for service of process, and [Name] is appointed chief compliance officer for AEO security audit services; and (v) all filing fees are authorized. This resolution becomes effective upon registration by ServiceOntario.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario Business Registry Online (nuans.com authorized intermediaries)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a NUANS name search request for the proposed limited partnership name. Review the preliminary search report for identical or confusingly similar names. Obtain consent from any conflicting name holder if required. Reserve the name using the online Ontario business name reservation portal if needed.
required_dossiers: Completed NUANS name search request form
Proposed partnership name and legal names of all general partners
Contact and authorization letter from proposed general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused, file a revised name selection or provide letters of consent from the conflicting party; resubmit the name search request without additional fee where an amendment is made within the validity period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: ServiceOntario, Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership. Identify the general partner(s), limited partners, principal place of business in Ontario, registered office address, and agent for service. Ensure the registered office is a physical address in Ontario and the agent for service is appointed in writing.
required_dossiers: Signed Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (Form 1)
NUANS name search report (less than 90 days old)
General partner's declaration and appointment of initial agent for service
Consent of the named agent to accept service
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ServiceOntario issues a Notice of Deficiency, provide corrected or supplementary documents within the stated cure period and resubmit electronically; expedited correction is available by telephone or in-person support.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submit Registration and Pay Statutory Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Log in to the ServiceOntario business registry portal, upload the application package, and pay the prescribed government fee using a corporate card or pre-authorized payment method. Upon successful processing, obtain the official limited partnership registration certificate and registration number.
required_dossiers: Completed application form set from Step 2
Proof of payment for registration fee
Digital copies of identity documents for signing general partner
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is rejected for incomplete information, amend the specific flagged fields and resubmit online within 15 days; no new name search is required if the name remains unchanged and the original NUANS report is valid.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register for Business Number and Tax Accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency – Business Registration Online
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership for a CRA Business Number (BN), GST/HST account if taxable revenue is anticipated, and payroll accounts if employees are hired. Designate an authorized representative. If the partnership has non-resident partners, file appropriate federal and provincial partnership information under income tax requirements.
required_dossiers: Partnership agreement (for internal reference, if requested by CRA)
Completed RC159 or online registration forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If CRA rejects the BN application because of a missing attestation, file the missing attestation online or tu via e-file; use the CRA Business Registration hotline to resolve mismatches between partnership name and registry record.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adopt Governance Documents and File Post-Registration Declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold a general partner meeting to ratify the limited partnership agreement, execute initial officer and compliance officer appointments, and sign all banking and client engagement documents. If any changes to general partners, limited partners, registered office, or agent for service occur, file the prescribed Declaration of Change with ServiceOntario.
required_dossiers: First general partner resolution and officer appointment consents
Statement of the registered office and agent for service filed with the registry
Bank account opening documents and AML/KYC forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If ServiceOntario queries a Declaration of Change, file a corrected declaration with the exact legal name and registration number; late declarations are cured by filing the corrective document without penalty if made within the regulatory grace period.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - Business Registration Online (BRO) and My Business Account portal; Ontario Ministry of Finance for Ontario provincial component of HST, administered by the CRA under the harmonized tax collection agreement.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign entity establishing an Ontario Limited Partnership does not receive a separate corporate TIN; the Canadian business tax identifier is the 9-digit Business Number (BN). The non-resident general partner or authorized representative must complete CRA registration through Business Registration Online (BRO) or submit Form RC1, and may open a GST/HST account, payroll account, and import/export account under the same BN. The Ontario LP must also complete any applicable extra-provincial limited partnership registration with the Government of Ontario's Companies and Personal Property Security Branch. Written evidence of the LP agreement, confirmation of Ontario extra-provincial registration, and partner identification are required. CRA will issue a BN/GST/HST registration confirmation letter; there is no separate VAT-ID document.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not provide a U.S.-style check-the-box election. For income tax, the Ontario Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent under section 96 of the Income Tax Act; the partnership files information return T5013 and partners report their allocated income/loss. For GST/HST purposes, the LP is generally a separate registrable person. Available elections include the joint GST/HST election under section 273 of the Excise Tax Act for qualifying closely related registrants (nil-consideration treatment of intercompany supplies), and partnership allocations may be made by the limited partnership agreement. Hybrid entity mismatch provisions under the enacted hybrid mismatch rules and the Income Tax Application Rules may deny benefits where jurisdictionally inconsistent tax treatment exists.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax); Ontario applies a single HST rate combining the 5% federal GST and 8% provincial PST component.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 (taxable supplies made in Canada per calendar quarter or over twelve consecutive months, whichever determination makes the person no longer a small supplier; once exceeded, GST/HST registration is mandatory)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada does not mandate real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory continuous transaction controls. Electronic invoicing is voluntary; CRA publishes the Pan-Canadian Trust Framework and supports the Peppol BIS 3.0 standard. Registrants above mandatory electronic filing thresholds must file GST/HST returns electronically via GST/HST NETFILE or through an EDI/software service. Books and records, including export documentation and electronic invoices, must be retained in a readable and accessible format and provided to CRA upon audit. No API-based clearance stamp is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of goods may be zero-rated under the Excise Tax Act where the goods are physically exported in accordance with the conditions in Schedule VI, Part V, generally requiring export to occur within a prescribed period and proof of export. Services supplied to non-residents are zero-rated under Schedule VI, Part V, section 7 or related provisions when the supply is for use wholly outside Canada, does not relate to real property located in Canada, and the non-resident is not registered for GST/HST. For audited supply-chain compliance services, zero-rating requires the contractual service to be genuinely performed for a non-resident beneficiary and not consumed in Canada.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA export declaration (Form B13A and electronic CADEX/ACI e-manifest data)
Ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or other transport document evidencing export out of Canada
Commercial invoice describing goods or services and showing zero-rated export treatment
Inward remittance evidence (SWIFT credit statement or bank transfer confirmation; Canada does not issue a formal inward remittance certificate)
Destination and foreign buyer documentation, including HS codes and consignee details
Export accounting records and reconciliation to the GST/HST return and ITC claims
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA may disallow zero-rating and claw back related input tax credits if documentary evidence is insufficient, untimely, or inconsistent. False or negligent export claims attract interest under section 280 of the Excise Tax Act, civil penalties for false statements or omissions under section 285, gross negligence penalties under section 327(6), revocation of registration, and criminal prosecution with fines and imprisonment. CBSA may also issue non-compliance penalties and assess forfeitures under customs legislation. Retroactive reassessment periods are generally four years from the date of assessment, but may be unlimited where misrepresentation, neglect, or wilful default is established.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) for transaction monitoring and the Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for customs-adjacent trade controls; no dedicated foreign exchange administration body exists in Canada.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains a fully convertible currency with no separate United States-style exchange control statutes. Both current account transactions (trade in goods and services, interest, dividends, royalties) and capital account transactions (foreign direct investment, portfolio capital, repatriation) are freely permitted without prior Bank of Canada approval. Profit remittance for a non-resident partner in an Ontario Limited Partnership is unrestricted upon satisfaction of anti-money-laundering verification, tax withholding obligations under the Canada-Ontario taxation framework, and the completion of T106 information returns for non-resident partners. Any amount may be converted to CAD or foreign currency on the open interbank market.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory timeline or mandatory conversion ratio applies to export receipts in Canada. Export proceeds may be retained in any currency, held offshore, or repatriated at the discretion of the entity, provided that the related transactions are not subject to suspicion-based reporting under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA). Standard recordkeeping obligations require retention of all underlying customs, invoice, and wire transfer documents for at least five years.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Medium with strict boundaries. Offshore electronic money institutions (EMIs) operating without any Canadian regulatory footprint generally cannot clear CAD-denominated payments into the domestic Canadian payment ecosystem without using an intermediary Canadian bank partner. Legitimate EMIs that hold a money-services business (MSB) registration with FINTRAC (or are a registered foreign MSB with nominal presence) and are also licensed in a CPC-0 equivalent jurisdiction may support inbound/outbound wires and FX settlement for the audit firm's supply-chain payment flows. Regardless of EMI suitability, all Canadian-dollar funding and disbursement rails must ultimately touch a Canadian-chartered bank or a registered Canadian clearing agent for the purpose of Beneficial Ownership reporting under PCMLTFA. Therefore, the LP should maintain one primary Canadian bank account as the anchor rail, with an EMI used only for low-value subcontractor remittances and non-resident supplier reimbursements.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permitted for Canadian banks under FINTRAC guidance, but the final discretion rests with each bank's compliance team. For a Limited Partnership, each General Partner whose signature is on the account and any directors/officers of a corporate General Partner must provide 100-point identification. Many Tier-1 banks require at least one principal (General Partner or designated signing officer) to complete an initial video-verification interview and, in high-risk cases, a physical in-branch visit at a Canadian or foreign correspondent branch. Given the low AML risk tier of the AEO audit business and the domestic nature of the Ontario LP, remote onboarding with video identity verification will likely suffice, subject to enhanced due diligence if any non-resident individual ultimately controls the partnership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Entity classification as a Limited Partnership with non-resident limited partners
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) notarized certificate of limited partnership from Ontario registry; (2) the full partnership agreement with capital contribution schedule; (3) a Limited Partner register identifying each partner's name, jurisdiction, and control status; (4) declaration that all partners are compliant with FINTRAC recordkeeping; (5) T106 Information Return for Non-Resident Partners or approved exemption rationale; (6) ultimate beneficial ownership table for any corporate partners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Customs AEO / supply-chain audit scope may be misclassified as high-risk trade sector requiring trade sanction screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit: (1) dated client engagement letters showing audit-only advisory scope, with no freight forwarding, customs brokerage, or physical goods movement; (2) CBSA AEO self-assessment certificate or proof of active application; (3) cybersecurity and Data Processing Agreement (DPA) confirming audited client data is held and destroyed in compliance with PIPEDA; (4) a negative sanctions match report from authoritative screening lists (OSFI, FINTRAC, UN, global PEP lists).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds for initial capital injection in capital escrow account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) bank statement of contributing partnership account for the preceding 6 months; (2) audit trail linking each capital contribution to partner name, date, and purpose; (3) signed undertakings confirming all contributions originate from lawful advisory fees, sale of goods, or inter-partner loans; (4) if amounts exceed CAD $10,000, FINTRAC large cash transaction report (LCTR) or wire summary, as applicable.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Signing authority and purported remote control by a US shareholder or foreign corporate general partner
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) resolutions appointing the Canadian resident General Manager or resident signing officer with power over outgoing wires above CAD $5,000; (2) proof of adequate tangible nexus through an Ontario registered office and client-facing establishment; (3) Canadian Goods and Services Tax/Harmonized Sales Tax (GST/HST) registration certificate; (4) the partnership's complete org chart of all partners and beneficial owners.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For non-resident partner capital contributions, the routing should use SWIFT MT103 to the partnership's Tier-1 account with the following clearing and reference protocol: SWIFT Instruction Code: CRED (credit reporting) with Consolidated FB (statement narrative) containing the Ontario Registration Number and entity legal name; CAD remittance purpose codes per the Canadian Financial Transactions Classification should reference T545 (wire transfer for partnership capital account), T001 (trade in services), or T502 (investment income redistribution), though Canada does not mandate a sector-specific mandatory purpose code; FINTRAC requires that the originating bank's details and complete Beneficial Ownership information be captured for any transfer exceeding CAD $3,000. To mitigate cross-border friction, first route the contribution via a Canadian clearing bank's foreign correspondent, then execute internal domestic clearing through the Canadian High Value Clearing and Settlement System (HVCS). Continuous Linked Settlement is not available for CAD in this flow; use traditional correspondent banking.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For trade settlements and supply-chain audit supplier payments, the primary clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 via the commercial bank's cross-border payment channel. For CAD domestic payments to enrolled vendors, use the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) via Payment Canada, or Real-Time Rail (RTR) if instant final payment is required. For USD-denominated settlement to overseas suppliers, the recommended methodology is either: (1) SWIFT MT103 through the bank's USD correspondent network (potentially via an intermediary like The Bank of New York Mellon or JPMorgan); or (2) a Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) issued under UCP600 for payments above CAD $50,000 that are contingent on presentation of Canadian customs documents, security audit fulfilment certificates, and bills of lading. For non-CAD and non-USD cross-border settlement, a supplementary Wise Business account may be used strictly for low-value vendor remittances below CAD $5,000, with enforcement of a documented written policy stating that any payment above this threshold must flow through the anchor commercial bank.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Canadian Dollar (CAD/USD) deliverable forward contracts (Plain Vanilla Forwards)
CAD-based currency swaps executed with an Ontario-registered Canadian Schedule I bank
Over-the-counter foreign exchange options involving CAD (with a licensed investment dealer holding a registration under the Ontario Securities Commission)

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) referencing CAD underlying exposure only if executed through a regulated Canadian dealer and physically settled if necessary; NDFs are less common in Canada due to both USD/CAD being a fully convertible pair
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (CCIRS) for converting long-term non-resident partner loans into CAD-denominated borrowings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Ontario Limited Partnership Annual Return (Corporations Information Act, R.S.O. 1990, c. C.39)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Public and Business Service Delivery and Procurement (ServiceOntario) — Companies and Personal Property Security Branch
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after the end of the partnership's fiscal year (e.g., 1-2 March if the fiscal year ends on 31 December).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No automatic monetary late fee; however, non-compliance is an offence under the Corporations Information Act. Continued failure after written notice from ServiceOntario can lead to administrative cancellation of the limited partnership registration and loss of the ability to lawfully carry on business in Ontario; each defaulting partner is also subject to summary conviction fines of up to CAD 2,000.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal Partnership Information Return (T5013 Summary and T5013 slips)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before 31 March following the calendar year in which the partnership's fiscal period ends.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day per return (minimum CAD 100; maximum CAD 2,500), plus possible gross-negligence penalties, interest, CRA garnishment and liens. There is no registry strike-off; prolonged non-filing triggers CRA compliance demands and recorded enforcement.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: GST/HST Return (if the LP is a GST/HST registrant or is required to be registered)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For an annual filer, within one month after the LP's fiscal year-end; if a quarterly or monthly filer, within one month of the end of each reporting period.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the unremitted amount plus 1% per full month of delay (maximum 12 months); CRA may assess interest, issue a federal tax lien, garnish bank accounts, or prosecute continued wilful evasion. Registrations may also be adjusted or cancelled by CRA after repeated non-filing.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No universal statutory audit is imposed on an Ontario limited partnership merely because it is an LP. An independent certified audit is compulsory when (i) the LP is a reporting issuer under Ontario securities law; (ii) it is subject to a contractual or regulator-imposed audit (e.g., CBSA/Canada Border Services Agency AEO-contract requirement, lender covenant, or insurer); (iii) the LP agreement or unanimous consent of partners requires an audit; or (iv) the general partner is a corporation whose federal or provincial corporate law or shareholder agreement imposes an audit on consolidated financial statements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: If financial statements are prepared, they are to be prepared in accordance with International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as published in CPA Canada Handbook Part I, or Canadian Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) under CPA Canada Handbook Part II for a non-public LP. Income and capital allocations are measured in Canadian dollars and computed under the partnership's fiscal period and the Income Tax Act allocation rules.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Ontario does not maintain a public UBO register for limited partnerships; the annual confirmation is therefore an internal corporate-governance and tax rule. Annually, no later than the closing of the fiscal year, the general partner must: reconcile the register of limited partners with transfers recorded during the year; obtain written beneficial-ownership confirmations (name, residential address, percentage interest, source of capital) from each limited partner; verify that any assignment of an LP interest was approved in accordance with the Ontario Limited Partnerships Act and the LP agreement; update the records of contributions, withdrawals and capital account allocations; file an Ontario Declaration of Change with ServiceOntario if the transfer changed partner identity or capital contribution particulars; retain KYC/AML documentation, especially for non-resident transferees; and re-issue T5013 allocation schedules on the corrected year-end ownership percentages.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (statutory under Ontario Limited Partnerships Act)
Register of General Partners and General-Partner Consents
Partnership minute book and records maintained at the registered office (including executed LP agreements, transfers and indemnity arrangements)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 180-450 per year (CAD 250-600) for a standard Ontario registered office/agent service with compliance support
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 2,500-7,500 for a small/medium private LP audit under ASPE; USD 7,000-18,000 if IFRS or audited supply-chain workpapers/customs AEO security testing are included in scope

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 26.5% combined federal (15%) + Ontario (11.5%) general corporate rate; LP is not a taxable person but each partner is taxed on allocable income
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Ontario small business rate of 3.2% and federal small business rate of 9% are available only to Canadian-controlled private corporations (CCPCs); limited partnership income generally passes through to partners and is not eligible for the SBD for specified members. AEO certification fees qualify as ordinary business income; no specific industry tax holiday; federal IM&T credit and Ontario strategic certificate of investment credits may apply to qualifying capital expenditures, but not to consulting fees.
